prs.title: Expose guarded NetworkTools split-point automation
prs.body:
Adds `nt_split` to the bridge client, dispatcher and command catalog so the regression runner can pin ordinary intermediate NetworkTools nodes using the current tool session/revision. Requires the companion NetworkTools split-point implementation; catalog presence alone is not successful integration.

Retains the existing sprint commits, including the separately authored MCP feasibility and latency investigation documents. No MCP server or latency optimization is implemented here.

Validation: installed native API contracts and the 61-command catalog passed again during packaging. Split control was exercised with native preview and permanent Apply during the sprint; details are in docs/session-notes/2026-09-29-0030-autonomous-sprint.md. No new deployment or game mutation during packaging.

Merge this bridge PR before exercising split cases from the NetworkTools stack.

Original incremental experiments (including unsuccessful approaches) remain intact in the [sprint history archive](https://github.com/danwayneharris/CS2-NetworkTools/tree/dan/autonomous-regressions). Review branches organize final snapshots without rewriting that history.


### Sprint PR stack

- Bridge: https://github.com/danwayneharris/cities2-agent-bridge-ndc/pull/5 — `dan/bridge-split-automation` → `main`
- NetworkTools: https://github.com/danwayneharris/CS2-NetworkTools/pull/7 — `dan/regression-harness` → `main`
- NetworkTools: https://github.com/danwayneharris/CS2-NetworkTools/pull/8 — `dan/split-point-smoothing` → `dan/regression-harness`
- NetworkTools: https://github.com/danwayneharris/CS2-NetworkTools/pull/9 — `dan/interior-junction-smoothing` → `dan/split-point-smoothing`
- NetworkTools: https://github.com/danwayneharris/CS2-NetworkTools/pull/10 — `dan/smoothing-research` → `dan/interior-junction-smoothing`

Merge the NetworkTools PRs in the listed order. After each lower PR merges, retarget the next PR to main if GitHub has not done so automatically. Keeping merge commits for the stack avoids ancestry loss from squash-merging a lower branch. No PR has been merged by this task.

prs.title: Bring merged automation milestone into main
prs.body:
## Behavior

Enables the local automation loop: a visible experimental launch helper extracts the save metadata identity and loads the exact toy save, opt-in remembered bridge controls survive restart, and six fixed NetworkTools commands forward to its Debug adapter. Controls remain off by default; STOP revokes permission. The adapter requires a paused city, rejects concurrent construction, and never exposes arbitrary reflection invocation.

Carries the already-reviewed #3 milestone into main. #2 merged first, then #3 merged into its former parent branch; consequently those later commits were not included in main. This follow-up preserves the existing commits without rewriting history. Companion NetworkTools changes provide the versioned adapter.

## Validation

- Bridge build and 60-command dispatcher/client/catalog checks passed.
- Save metadata regression checks passed; successful visible launch loaded a verified unique checkpoint. Remembered controls restored on startup.
- Live NetworkTools activation, selection, 0.5-to-0.8 strength change, stale-request rejection and Apply succeeded.
- Independent permanent readback in NetworkTools preserved all four rail connections and exactly matched incident preview curves; maintainer visual check positive.
- Experiment notes include failed hidden launch/control restoration attempts and their corrections.

## Limits

Experimental Windows launch path, tested on one local setup and one toy rail case. Not a general unattended gameplay guarantee. Clear, malformed requests, STOP revocation and remember-off restart need broader live coverage. Existing full mailbox suite was not completed (local .NET/PowerShell harness constraints); compilation is not a substitute. Apply acceptance requires subsequent state and permanent-geometry verification. No Paradox release publication.

prs.title: Record verified connected-preview resolver deployment and live evidence
prs.body:
Reconcile the connected-preview resolver's deployment checkpoint and documentation with live NetworkTools tests. Shared-endpoint resolution exposed a four-to-three connection loss in the old preview; corrected preview and Apply retained all four.

This branch contains deployment/evidence documentation, not a new resolver implementation. Snapshot completeness remains distinct from tool freshness, and validationReady remains false. No launch/load/save or generic mod-control capability is claimed.

prs.title: Add junction snapshots and topology-based preview discovery
prs.body:
Junction investigation needs native lane and composition evidence, and matching preview nodes by Temp.m_Original can return a disconnected copy. This adds paused, read-only junction snapshots, independent preview-edge discovery, and a resolver that identifies the connected temporary junction through shared endpoints of mapped incident edges. Missing and ambiguous results remain explicit; validationReady remains false.

Includes query/API documentation, local build instructions, contract tests, and chronological experiment notes. The startup helper is retained as a documented investigation, with -Launch disabled after a failed platform-initialization test.

Validation recorded during development: bridge build, native API contract checks, command registration checks, and actual C# resolver tests against captured evidence passed. Earlier snapshot/edge queries were exercised in-game. The newest connectedSnapshot resolver is compiled and offline-tested but NOT deployed or live-verified. No automatic Apply authorization or reliable unattended launch/load workflow is claimed.

Next supervised test: deploy with CS2 closed, load the paused toy save, and inspect the connected preview junction and its native lanes. Companion NetworkTools investigation PR records the captures and geometry analysis. This PR targets our fork only.
